diff: With Part I's hypotheses the topology is the unique one of `theorem_12_5_3_hyp`. "Smooth morphism" is read as a morphism with smooth source and target (equivalent by `mem_smoothSet_src_iff`).

items.title: Proposition 12.5.6 (2017: 12.4), orientability through $|\sigma|$

book.label: §12.5, Proposition 12.5.6, p. 595 (2017: Proposition 12.4)
book.statement: $f$ is orientable if and only if $|\sigma| : |O_f| \to |X_\infty|$ is two-to-one and has a global continuous section.

lean.statement: `EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mp`: an orientation (`definition_12_5_4 t o`) gives `IsTwoToOne` and a continuous section of `orbitProj`. `proposition_12_5_6_mpr_invariant`: from `IsTwoToOne` and any section $s$ of $|\sigma|$, a section $o$ of $\sigma$ with $\varphi_* o_x = o_{x'}$ for all morphisms, lifting $s$. Orbit spaces: quotients by `SmoothRel` and `OrRel`.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: `hsec`, as in V12.22.
(⇒) is complete. (⇐) is proved without the continuity of $o$, which needs the last clause of Theorem 12.5.3 (gaps G.138, G.139). The orbit spaces are quotients defined here.

items.title: Complete fibre norms are automatic (tool)

book.label: not in the book (used for Definition 5.1.1 (1) and Definition 12.2.1 (1))
book.statement: The text asserts that the glued fibre norms are complete.

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_of_tendsto`: a continuous fibrewise seminorm with property (2) of Definition 5.1.1 is an auxiliary norm, since near each point it is squeezed between multiples of the chart norm $|\cdot|_1$.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 12.2.7, the local extension of an auxiliary norm from $\partial X$
notFormalized.label: §12.2, Theorem 12.2.7, pp. 574–576 (local step, p. 575) (2017: Theorem 12.3)
notFormalized.book: Near $x_0 \in \partial X$, in a tame local model with $O \subset [0,\infty)^n \oplus H$ and retraction $R(u,w) = (r(u), A(u)w)$, with $q(t,h) = (t,h) - \min(t)(1,\dots,1,0)$: $r \circ q$ maps a neighbourhood of $x_0$ into $\partial O$, and $N'(u,w) = N(rq(u), A(rq(u))w) + \|w - A(rq(u))w\|_{F_1}$ is a local auxiliary norm equal to $N$ over $\partial X$.
notFormalized.instead: `EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp` takes exactly this local step as the hypothesis `HasLocalExtensions X B N` (V12.9); the rest of the proof is formalized. Missing: (a) a tame strong bundle chart around every boundary point (the project's strong bundle charts are not known to have tame base retractions), about 500–1,000 lines; (b) the map $r \circ q$ with its continuity and boundary properties in quadrant coordinates, about 300–500 lines; (c) the level-1 continuity of $u \mapsto A(u)$ and conditions (1)–(2) for $N'$, about 500–1,000 lines. Total about 1,300–2,500 lines.

notFormalized.title: Definition 12.3.6, the ep-groupoid form
notFormalized.label: §12.3, Definition 12.3.6, p. 584 (2017: Definition 12.8)
notFormalized.book: An sc⁺-section over the boundary of a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid.
notFormalized.instead: The chart-level form (`IsBoundaryScPlusSectionOn`, V12.16) and the M-polyfold form (`StrongBundle.IsBoundaryScPlusSection`, V5.88, applicable to the object M-polyfold) exist. A named ep-groupoid wrapper, the M-polyfold form on objects with the remark that it does not involve $\mu$, is about 30 lines; it belongs with Theorem 12.3.9 (wave 2).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 12.5.3, last sentence: morphisms keep local orientation sections continuous
notFormalized.label: §12.5, Theorem 12.5.3, last sentence, p. 594 (2017: Theorem 12.11)
notFormalized.book: For a morphism $\varphi : x \to x'$ between smooth points, the local $\hat\Phi$ pushes a continuous local section of $\sigma$ to a continuous local section.
notFormalized.instead: Not formalized. It needs the naturality of Part I's path transport (`LocalTransport`, `IsContOrOn`) under the local strong bundle isomorphism `EpStrongBundle.morIso`: for an sc-smooth path near $x'$, transport along it commutes with `orVia` along its image. The pointwise data exist (`StrongBundle.LocalIso.orVia`, `orVia_eq`, `morT_comp`; V12.22); missing is the comparison of Part I's propagation charts with pulled charts along a path. Estimate 1,000–1,500 lines.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐), continuity of the orientation
notFormalized.label: §12.5, Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐), p. 595 (2017: Proposition 12.4)
notFormalized.book: If $|\sigma|$ is two-to-one and has a global continuous section, $f$ is orientable.
notFormalized.instead: `EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mpr_invariant` gives the functorial section $o$ lifting the section of $|\sigma|$ (V12.26); its continuity for Part I's topology is not proved. It follows from G.138 ($O_f \to |O_f|$ is then a local homeomorphism near each point, and $o$ agrees locally with a continuous germ). Estimate 300–500 lines after G.138.

notFormalized.title: §12.5 with a tame $X$ only: Part I's bump functions and tame germ data
notFormalized.label: §12.5, Theorem 12.5.3, p. 594 (2017: Theorem 12.11)
notFormalized.book: The orientation bundle and its topology for an sc-Fredholm section functor over a tame ep-groupoid, with no further hypothesis.
notFormalized.instead: `EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_5_3_hyp` (V12.24) carries the hypotheses of Part I's Theorem 6.6.17, `hbump : X.PObj.AdmitsBumpFunctions` and the tame germ data `hfT : B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f`, passed through unchanged, and Lemma 12.5.1 and Proposition 12.5.6 take `hsec : B.HasScPlusSectionsThrough` (a consequence of bump functions). These are Part I's inherited hypotheses (rows V6.74, V6.75), not new ones; removing them needs Part I's orientation transport without bump functions and for untamed germ data.
